title: What Earth's horizon costs
summary: At the south pole Earth sits low on the horizon and ridges hide it. With direct links only, the base delivers {{r:dte_loss}} less cargo a year, mostly because one work site never sees Earth. A part-time relay or more autonomy fixes it; more rovers do not.
summary_plain: At the south pole Earth sits low on the horizon and ridges hide it. With direct links only, the base delivers 42 % less cargo a year, mostly because one work site never sees Earth. A part-time relay or more autonomy fixes it; more rovers do not.
notes: E21 (experiments/phase4/run_phase4.py, analysis experiments/phase4/analyse_e21.py): P2 six-rover fleet, marketplace, pads 1 km, no plume, 20 seeds per cell, start years 2028-2031. Wording by LEAD, 22 Oct 2026.

always_t.source: results/table_E21.csv, row stage = A, comms = always, mix = supervised_strict, column delivered_t_in_year; Earth always in view, all supervised rovers, strict policy (E21 stage A)
always_t.label: Delivered with Earth always in view

dte_t.source: results/table_E21.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strict, column delivered_t_in_year; direct-to-Earth links only (E21 stage A)
dte_t.label: Delivered with direct links only

dte_loss.source: pct_change of always_t and dte_t (unrounded); neg
dte_loss.label: Lost against Earth always in view

base_link.source: results/E21_fit.json: throughput/site_link_fraction_dte_any_part/BASE; x 100; share of 2028-2031 in which any part of Earth's disc is above the terrain horizon at the base, 2.5 m antenna (B-40)
base_link.label: Time Earth is in view at the base

isru_lost.source: results/E21_fit.json: throughput/lost_at_never_linked_t/mean; cargo bound for the ISRU plant that is never delivered under direct links only (E21 analysis)
isru_lost.label: ISRU cargo never delivered

dte_wait.source: results/table_E21.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strict, column blackout_wait_vehicle_h; rover time spent waiting for Earth in the year
dte_wait.label: Rover time spent waiting for Earth

relay_t.source: results/table_E21.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte+relay, coverage = 0.1, mix = supervised_strict, column delivered_t_in_year; a relay satellite in view a tenth of the time, besides direct links
relay_t.label: Delivered, relay a tenth of the time

auto_t.source: results/table_E21.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = autonomous, column delivered_t_in_year; direct links only, fully autonomous rovers
auto_t.label: Delivered by autonomous rovers

rover_gain.source: results/table_E21_breakeven.csv, row option = +1 supervised LTV, column gain_vs_dte; gain of one extra supervised LTV over direct links only (E21 stage B)
rover_gain.label: Gain from one extra supervised rover

half_strict.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay.csv, row option = +1 rover, column base_value; urgent cargo: hours within which 90 % is delivered, relay in view half the time, strict supervision (E21 stage B)
half_strict.label: Half relay: one in ten urgent waits over

half_plus1.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay.csv, row option = +1 rover, column value; the same with one extra rover
half_plus1.label: The same with one extra rover

half_strategic.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay.csv, row option = strategic step, column value; the same with supervised rovers that drive between check-ins on their own (strategic policy)
half_strategic.label: The same with strategic driving

rover_dp.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay.csv, row option = +1 rover, column delta_p; x 100; relay coverage that gives the same urgent delay as one extra rover, at half coverage (bootstrap over seeds)
rover_dp.label: Relay coverage worth one extra rover

strategic_dp.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay.csv, row option = strategic step, column delta_p; x 100; relay coverage that gives the same urgent delay as the strategic policy, at half coverage
strategic_dp.label: Relay coverage worth strategic driving

steps.title: Earth hangs on the horizon
steps.text: Seen from the south pole Earth never climbs high, and ridges hide it. From the base it is in view {{r:base_link}} of the time. A rover driven or supervised from Earth needs that link.
steps.visual: Earth low over the ridge; the terrain shadow marks where it is hidden.
steps.text_plain: Seen from the south pole Earth never climbs high, and ridges hide it. From the base it is in view 59 % of the time. A rover driven or supervised from Earth needs that link.
steps.visual_plain: Earth low over the ridge; the terrain shadow marks where it is hidden.

steps.title: Waiting for Earth
steps.text: With direct links only, rovers spend {{r:dte_wait}} a year parked, waiting for Earth to rise.
steps.visual: Rovers parked in the waiting colour while Earth is below the ridge.
steps.text_plain: With direct links only, rovers spend 972 rover-hours a year parked, waiting for Earth to rise.
steps.visual_plain: Rovers parked in the waiting colour while Earth is below the ridge.

steps.title: The cargo it costs
steps.text: The base delivers {{r:dte_t}} instead of {{r:always_t}}: {{r:dte_loss}} less.
steps.visual: The delivery counter of the year, with and without the horizon.
steps.text_plain: The base delivers 307 t per year instead of 532 t per year: 42 % less.
steps.visual_plain: The delivery counter of the year, with and without the horizon.

steps.title: One site never sees Earth
steps.text: Most of that loss is one place. The plant that makes oxygen from regolith sits where Earth is never in view, so {{r:isru_lost}} of cargo for it never arrives. No rover driven from Earth can work there.
steps.visual: The ISRU site highlighted; its route drawn in the colour for no link.
steps.text_plain: Most of that loss is one place. The plant that makes oxygen from regolith sits where Earth is never in view, so 204 t per year of cargo for it never arrives. No rover driven from Earth can work there.
steps.visual_plain: The ISRU site highlighted; its route drawn in the colour for no link.

steps.title: A relay, or autonomy
steps.text: A relay satellite in view only a tenth of the time brings deliveries back to {{r:relay_t}}. Fully autonomous rovers reach {{r:auto_t}} with no relay at all.
steps.visual: A relay link drawn from the rovers to a satellite passing over.
steps.text_plain: A relay satellite in view only a tenth of the time brings deliveries back to 530 t per year. Fully autonomous rovers reach 532 t per year with no relay at all.
steps.visual_plain: A relay link drawn from the rovers to a satellite passing over.

steps.title: More rovers cannot buy it back
steps.text: One more supervised rover adds {{r:rover_gain}}: it waits for Earth like the others.
steps.visual: The fleet with an extra rover, parked in the waiting colour.
steps.title_plain: More rovers cannot buy it back
steps.text_plain: One more supervised rover adds 0.6 t per year: it waits for Earth like the others.
steps.visual_plain: The fleet with an extra rover, parked in the waiting colour.

steps.title: Autonomy is worth more than a rover
steps.text: With a relay in view half the time, nine in ten urgent items arrive within {{r:half_strict}}. One more rover brings that to {{r:half_plus1}}. Letting supervised rovers drive on their own between check-ins brings it to {{r:half_strategic}}. In relay terms the rover is worth {{r:rover_dp}} and the autonomy step {{r:strategic_dp}}.
steps.visual: Three bars: the fleet as it is, one more rover, and the autonomy step.
steps.title_plain: Autonomy is worth more than a rover
steps.text_plain: With a relay in view half the time, nine in ten urgent items arrive within 40 h. One more rover brings that to 31 h. Letting supervised rovers drive on their own between check-ins brings it to 27 h. In relay terms the rover is worth 18 percentage points of relay coverage and the autonomy step 29 percentage points of relay coverage.
steps.visual_plain: Three bars: the fleet as it is, one more rover, and the autonomy step.
